questions.q: Simon defined learning as changes in a system that result in ____ over time on tasks similar to those done previously.
questions.explanation: Herbert Simon defined learning as changes in a system that make it perform the same or similar tasks more effectively the next time, i.e. improved performance over time.

a change that persists over a period of time
a change not simply ascribable to processes of growth
questions.explanation: Gagne's definition has all three parts: learning is a change in human disposition or capability, it persists over a period of time, and it is not simply ascribable to processes of growth.
The psychomotor domain of Bloom's taxonomy covers physical (manual or motor) skills such as movement, coordination and manipulation; cognitive and mental skills belong to the cognitive domain.

options: re-examining experience in the light of one's intent and existing knowledge
using helpful feelings and removing obstructive ones
questions.explanation: In Boud, Keogh and Walker's reflection model, returning to experience means recalling or detailing the salient events. Attending to feelings (using helpful ones, removing obstructive ones) and re-evaluating the experience are the later stages.

questions.q: Which of the following assumptions does not come under the behaviorist orientation to learning?
options: Differences between individuals are important as they will affect learning
Observable behavior rather than internal thought processes are the focus of study.
The principle of contiguity is central
questions.explanation: Behaviorism focuses on observable behavior, holds that the environment shapes behavior, and treats contiguity (and reinforcement) as central. Emphasising individual differences is not one of its core assumptions.

questions.q: Reinforcement can come through sharing of results rather than a reward.
questions.explanation: True. Reinforcement does not have to be a tangible reward: sharing results or giving feedback on performance can also strengthen the desired behavior.

questions.q: ____ has contributed to the humanistic orientations to learning.
questions.explanation: Carl Rogers, together with Abraham Maslow, is a key figure of the humanistic orientation, which stresses self-directed, experiential learning and personal growth. The other options are learning styles, not contributors.

questions.q: In the process of learning, which of the following is not a component of output?
questions.explanation: Outputs are the results of learning, such as certification, attitude change and knowledge enhancement. A training plan is an input or part of the process, not an output.

questions.q: Ambience, space and decorum do not affect learning.
questions.explanation: False. The physical learning environment, including ambience, space and decorum, affects attention, comfort and motivation, and therefore affects learning.

questions.q: Role-playing can motivate ____ type of learners effectively.
questions.explanation: Role-play is an interactive, group-based activity, so it suits social (interpersonal) learners who learn best by working with others.
